stages.title: Intermediate vocabulary
explain: Some Italian words look like English words but mean something different. They are called falsi amici (false friends). "Parenti" means relatives, not parents (those are "genitori"). "Camera" means room, not a photo camera. "Libreria" is a bookshop, while "biblioteca" is a library.
Many words are true cousins: "la nazione", "il ristorante", "importante". Learn word families too: "lavorare" (to work), "il lavoro" (work), "il lavoratore" (worker).
sentences: I buy a book at the bookshop.
We borrow books at the library.

gq.why: It is a false friend of English parents.

panel.q: Why are false friends dangerous?
o: They look familiar so the meaning is assumed wrongly
panel.why: Similar form does not guarantee similar meaning.

panel.q: Which word is a true cognate of English "important"?
panel.why: Importante has the same meaning.

panel.q: A learner says "Vado in camera per fare foto". What does this say?
o: I go to a room to take photos
I go to a camera shop
I take a camera to a room
panel.why: Camera means room; the camera is la macchina fotografica.

teach.model: False friends look like English words but have another meaning, like parenti for relatives. Word families link words, like lavorare, il lavoro and il lavoratore. Check unknown words.

stages.hook: The word "parenti" looks like "parents", but is it? Which Italian words can trick an English speaker?
stages.mnemonic: Parenti are relatives; genitori are parents.

stages.title: Verb forms and time expressions
explain: The passato prossimo is the usual past tense. It uses avere or essere plus a past participle: "Ho mangiato", "Sono andata". Verbs of movement and reflexive verbs use essere, and the participle agrees with the subject: "Lei è partita", "Loro sono partiti".

The futuro semplice changes the ending: "mangerò", "mangerai", "mangerà". Spoken Italian often uses the present for the near future: "Domani vado a Roma". Time words help: ieri (yesterday), oggi (today), domani (tomorrow), già (already), presto (soon).
sentences: Tomorrow we will travel by train.

gq.q: Choose the correct form: Ieri noi ___ al cinema.
gq.why: Andare uses essere in the passato prossimo.

gq.q: Why is it "Lei è partita" with -a?
o: The participle agrees with the subject when essere is used
gq.why: With essere the past participle agrees with the subject.

panel.q: What is the futuro semplice of "parlare" for tu?
panel.why: The -are endings change to -er in the future.

panel.q: Why is "Domani vado a Roma" correct?
o: Italian often uses the present for a planned future
panel.why: The present can express a scheduled future.

panel.q: Why does "Ho mangiato" not change for a woman?
o: With avere the participle normally stays the same
panel.why: Agreement with avere is only needed with some object pronouns.

points.ask: How do I form the past?
How do I say the future?

teach.model: For completed past actions use the passato prossimo: avere or essere plus a participle. Verbs of movement use essere and the participle agrees. The future changes the ending, like mangerò.

stages.hook: How do you say "I ate yesterday" and "I will eat tomorrow" in Italian?

stages.title: Complex sentence introduction
explain: Use conjunctions: "e" (and), "ma" (but), "o" (or), "perché" (because), "quando" (when), "se" (if), "affinché" (so that). Example: "Resto a casa perché piove."
"Che" links two clauses: "Penso che sia bello". It also works as a relative pronoun: "Il libro che leggo è bello." Use "chi" for "who" in questions.
sentences: I stay at home because it rains.
The book that I read is good.
If it rains, we stay here.

gq.q: Choose the correct word: Il libro ___ leggo è bello.
gq.why: Che links the noun libro to the clause.

gq.q: Why is "Penso che sia bello" with sia?
o: After pensare, che often takes the subjunctive
gq.why: Verbs of opinion often take the subjunctive.

panel.q: Which conjunction shows contrast?
panel.why: Ma means but.

panel.q: What does "benché" express?
panel.why: It introduces a contrast and takes the subjunctive.

panel.q: A learner says "Resto a casa perchè piove". What is wrong?
panel.why: Perché takes an acute accent, not a grave one.

teach.model: Conjunctions like e, ma, perché and quando join ideas. Che links clauses and can mean that, which or who. Benché and affinché take the subjunctive.

stages.hook: How do you join two ideas, such as "I stay home because it is raining"?
stages.mnemonic: Che does many jobs: that, which, who.

stages.title: Reading short stories
explain: Aesop and many Italian storytellers use animals to teach morals. The fable "Il lupo e l'agnello" shows a strong wolf who finds an excuse to attack a weak lamb. The moral is that those with power may invent reasons to do harm.

Italian stories often use the passato remoto in writing (disse, andò) and the imperfetto for the setting (faceva bel tempo). In speech, many speakers use the passato prossimo; in southern Italy, the passato remoto remains common. Reading skills: find who, where, when and what happens.
sentences: Once upon a time there was a king.

gq.q: How does a story traditionally begin in Italian?
gq.why: It is the classic opening and uses the imperfetto.

gq.q: Why is the imperfetto used in "faceva bel tempo"?
gq.why: The imperfetto sets scenes and continuing states.

panel.q: What is a fable?
o: A short story with animals and a moral
panel.why: Fables teach lessons through simple stories.

panel.q: Why is the passato remoto less common in northern speech?
o: The passato prossimo has replaced it in conversation
panel.why: Usage differs by region.

panel.q: What is the effect of "all'improvviso" in a story?
panel.why: Time markers guide the reader.

teach.model: In an Italian tale, find who, where, when and what happens. The imperfetto describes the scene and the passato prossimo or remoto tells events. Fables end with a moral.

stages.hook: Read this short tale about a wolf and a lamb. Who wins, and why?
stages.mnemonic: Imperfetto paints the scene; passato prossimo moves the plot.

stages.title: Listening comprehension
explain: When listening, do not translate every word. Catch the key words: numbers, names, places and time words. Predict from context: at a station you expect times, platforms and tickets.
Notice that Italian words run together: "c'è" and "l'ho" join vowels. Double consonants help meaning: "sete" (thirst) and "sette" (seven). Repeat audio at slower speed, then at normal speed.
sentences: The train leaves at eight o'clock.
Platform two is on the left.

gq.q: What is a good listening strategy?
o: Catch key words and use context
Stop listening if you miss a word
gq.why: Key words and context let you follow the meaning.

o: The double t changes the word

panel.q: At a station you hear "Il treno per Milano è in ritardo". What does it say?
o: The train to Milan is late
panel.why: In ritardo means late.

panel.q: Why is a double consonant important when listening?
o: It lengthens the sound and can change the word
panel.why: Gemination is meaningful in Italian.

panel.q: Why can two listeners understand the same announcement differently?
panel.why: Prediction from context affects comprehension.

teach.model: Listen for key words like numbers and places. Use context to guess. Notice double consonants and run-together vowels. Ask for repetition if needed.

stages.hook: You hear "Sono le otto e mezza." What helps you understand a fast spoken sentence?
stages.mnemonic: Hear the key words, guess the rest.

stages.title: Conversation and pronunciation
explain: The Italian r is rolled with the tip of the tongue. Double consonants are held: "pappa" (porridge) and "papa" (pope) are different. The groups "gli" and "gn" have special sounds: "figlio", "bagno". Vowels are clear, with no gliding.
Stress usually falls on the second-to-last syllable: "parLAre", "caPIto". Intonation rises on questions. Use fillers such as "allora", "dunque", "ecco" and "boh" to keep speech natural.
sentences: My son is in the bathroom.

gq.q: What difference do double consonants make in Italian?
gq.why: Pappa and papa are different words.

gq.q: Why is "gli" in "figlio" a good example of a special sound?
o: It stands for one sound like lli in million
It is said g plus l plus i
gq.why: Gli makes a palatal l sound.

panel.q: Where is the stress in "parlare"?
panel.why: Most Italian words have penultimate stress.

panel.q: What does "boh" express?
panel.why: It is an informal filler showing doubt.

panel.q: Why do English speakers make mistakes with "bagno"?
o: They say g plus n instead of one sound
panel.why: Gn is a single sound.

teach.model: Italian r is rolled. Double consonants are held and can change meaning, like papa and pappa. Gn and gli are single sounds. Stress usually falls on the second-to-last syllable.

stages.hook: How can you sound natural when speaking Italian? Which sounds are hardest?
stages.mnemonic: Roll the r, hold the double, keep the vowel pure.

stages.title: Writing paragraphs
explain: A paragraph has an opening sentence, support, and a closing sentence. Use linking words: "prima" (first), "poi" (then), "dopo" (after), "infine" (finally), "per esempio" (for example), "però" (however).
Check your writing for agreement, accents and verb endings. Example: "Prima mi alzo alle sette. Poi mangio del pane. Infine vado a scuola."
sentences: First I get up at seven.

gq.q: Why are linking words useful in a paragraph?
gq.why: Connectors show order, contrast or cause.

panel.q: Which connector shows contrast?
panel.why: Però means however.

panel.q: Which connector shows a result?
panel.why: Quindi means therefore.

panel.q: What is a good checking routine after writing?
o: Check agreement, accents, verb endings and spelling
panel.why: These are the typical sources of Italian errors.

teach.model: Begin with an opening sentence, then give support and end with a closing sentence. Use prima, poi and infine to order ideas, and però for contrast. Check agreement and accents.

stages.hook: How do you write a short paragraph in Italian that sounds connected?
stages.mnemonic: Prima, poi, infine: first, then, last.

stages.title: Cultural expressions and idioms
explain: "In bocca al lupo" (into the wolf's mouth) means good luck. The usual reply is "Crepi!" (may it die). Other idioms: "Avere le mani in pasta" (to have a hand in something), "Non avere peli sulla lingua" (to speak frankly), "Costare un occhio della testa" (to cost a fortune).

Cultural expressions include "Buon appetito" before eating and "Cin cin!" when raising a glass. Italians often greet friends with a kiss on each cheek, and shops traditionally close for the afternoon rest in some regions.
items: to have a hand in something

gq.q: What do you reply to "In bocca al lupo"?
Why is it a mistake to say "Grazie" to "In bocca al lupo" in the traditional exchange?
o: Thanking is said to bring bad luck; Crepi is used

panel.q: What do you say before a meal?
panel.why: Buon appetito is said before eating.

panel.q: What does "non avere peli sulla lingua" mean?
panel.why: It means not hiding what you think.

panel.q: Why do idioms help understanding of a culture?
o: They reflect shared images and experiences
panel.why: Idioms carry cultural history and humour.

points.ask: What does in bocca al lupo mean?
What do I say at meals?

teach.model: An idiom has a fixed meaning that differs from its words, like in bocca al lupo for good luck. Learn idioms as whole phrases. Say Buon appetito before a meal and Cin cin when you drink.

stages.hook: If someone says "In bocca al lupo!", are they wishing you harm?
stages.mnemonic: Do not translate idioms word for word; learn them as pictures.

stages.title: Practical travel communication
explain: Useful phrases: "Dov'è la stazione?", "Un biglietto, per favore", "A che ora parte il treno?" and "Cerco l'albergo." For directions: sempre dritto (straight on), a sinistra (left), a destra (right).
At a restaurant ask "Il conto, per favore." At a hotel say "Ho una prenotazione." In an emergency say "Aiuto!" and "Ho bisogno di aiuto." Politeness is key: begin with "Scusi" or "Buongiorno".
sentences: Excuse me, where is the station?
Turn left, then go straight on.

gq.q: You want directions. What do you say first?
Why is "Lei" used with a stranger?

panel.q: What does "sempre dritto" mean?
panel.why: Sempre dritto is straight ahead.

panel.q: Which phrase would you use in an emergency?
panel.why: Aiuto means help.

panel.q: Why start a request with "Buongiorno"?
o: In Italian culture greeting first is expected
panel.why: Skipping the greeting can seem impolite.

points.ask: How do I ask for help?

teach.model: Be polite: start with Buongiorno or Scusi, use Lei and say per favore. Ask directions with Dov'è? and understand sempre dritto, a sinistra and a destra. In an emergency say Aiuto.

stages.hook: You arrive in Rome and need a train ticket. What do you say?
stages.mnemonic: Scusi opens doors; grazie closes them.
